title: How is Hitler connected to Lionel Messi?
description: Six real photos connect Adolf Hitler to Lionel Messi, through his foreign minister, Stalin, Khrushchev, Fidel Castro and Argentina's president.
hook: How is Adolf Hitler connected to Lionel Messi?
fun_fact: When Khrushchev first met Fidel Castro in 1960, he drove up to Harlem's Hotel Theresa, where Castro had moved after a row with his Midtown hotel.
research_note: No free photo shows Ribbentrop with anyone who lived into Messi's era, so the chain leaves through his 1939 Kremlin handshake with Stalin; a Castro to Maradona to Messi ending would have needed two press photos, while Argentina's presidency photographed Cristina Kirchner with both Castro and Messi.

image.file: File:Podróż inspekcyjna Adolfa Hitlera w czasie kampanii wrześniowej (2-3).jpg

links.line: In 1939, during the invasion of Poland, foreign minister Joachim von Ribbentrop joined Hitler at his headquarters train.

image.file: File:Bundesarchiv Bild 183-H27337, Moskau, Stalin und Ribbentrop im Kreml.jpg

links.line: In 1939, Ribbentrop flew to Moscow and shook hands with Joseph Stalin at the Nazi-Soviet pact signing.
In the 1930s, Stalin's Moscow party boss was a rising star named Nikita Khrushchev.

image.credit: Herman Hiller, New York World-Telegram & Sun / Library of Congress

links.line: In 1960, Khrushchev and Fidel Castro met in New York during the United Nations General Assembly.

image.file: File:Cristina Fernández de Kircher y Fidel Castro - 2009.jpg

links.line: In 2009, Argentina's president, Cristina Kirchner, flew to Havana and met privately with Fidel Castro.

image.file: File:Cristina Fernández y la Selección Argentina de fútbol 2014 ,2.jpg

links.line: And in 2014, Cristina Kirchner welcomed home Argentina's World Cup captain, Lionel Messi.
